extracted.intended_audience: scholars and students of mathematics and natural philosophy; general readers of Newton's Principia
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted sections from Isaac Newton's Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica (Latin edition) containing the formal Definitions, Scholium (distinctions of absolute/relative time/space/etc.), Axioms/Laws of Motion and immediate corollaries; plus the Project Gutenberg distribution license appended to the eBook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Def. I — Quantitas Materiæ (Quantity of Matter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantitas Materiæ est mensura ejusdem orta ex illius Densitate & Magnitudine conjunctim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that quantity of matter (mass) is measured from both density and magnitude (volume); exemplified by how doubling density and space affects quantity, notes detectability via weight (pendulum experiments). Transcriber's notes clarify conventions (braces, overlining); Newton intends 'mass' as proportional to weight under experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Def. II — Quantitas motus (Quantity of Motion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantitas motus est mensura ejusdem orta ex Velocitate et quantitate Materiæ conjunctim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines 'quantity of motion' as the product of mass and velocity (momentum). Gives consequences for doubled mass/velocity combinations and how total motion is the sum over parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Def. III — Materiæ vis insita (Vis insita / Inertia)
rubrics_metrics.description: Materiæ vis insita est potentia resistendi, qua corpus unumquodq;, quantum in se est, perseverat in statu suo vel quiescendi vel movendi uniformiter in directum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterizes innate force (inertia) as the power to resist change of state (rest or uniform motion). Discusses relation to mass and distinguishes 'vis insita' as conceptual for mathematical treatment; explains roles of resistance and impetus when external force acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Def. IV — Vis impressa (Impressed Force)
rubrics_metrics.description: Vis impressa est actio in corpus exercita, ad mutandum ejus statum vel quiescendi vel movendi uniformiter in directum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines impressed force as an action exerted on a body to change its state; emphasizes it is an action and doesn't remain after action ceases (in contrast to vis insita). Gives examples (impulse, pressure, centripetal force).

rubrics_metrics.name: Def. V — Vis centripeta (Centripetal Force)
rubrics_metrics.description: Vis centripeta est qua corpus versus punctum aliquod tanquam ad centrum trahitur, impellitur, vel utcunq; tendit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies centripetal forces (gravity, magnetism, etc.) and notes they may be considered mathematically rather than physically in this context. Introduces three measures of centripetal force (absolute, accelerative, motive) to be defined next.

rubrics_metrics.name: Def. VI — Vis centripetæ quantitas absoluta (Absolute quantity of a centripetal force)
rubrics_metrics.description: Vis centripetæ quantitas absoluta est mensura ejusdem major vel minor pro efficacia causæ eam propagantis a centro per regiones in circuitu.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives idea of an absolute measure of force as a property of the cause at the center, independent of location; illustrative comparison (magnetic strength between magnets). Newton postpones physical causes, treating the concept mathematically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Def. VII — Vis centripetæ quantitas acceleratrix (Accelerating measure of centripetal force)
rubrics_metrics.description: Vis centripetæ quantitas acceleratrix est ipsius mensura Velocitati proportionalis, quam dato tempore generat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines accelerative measure as proportional to the velocity generated per unit time (acceleration). Uses examples: magnetism varying with distance, gravity varying with altitude (e.g., pendulum experiments). Notes relation between accelerative and motive measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Def. VIII — Vis centripetæ quantitas motrix (Motive quantity of centripetal force)
rubrics_metrics.description: Vis centripetæ quantitas motrix est ipsius mensura proportionalis motui, quem dato tempore generat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines motive measure as proportional to the motion (momentum) produced in a given time; relates motive force to weight (ponderosity) near Earth's surface and its variation with distance from center.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholium — Distinction between absolute and relative time, space, place and motion
rubrics_metrics.description: Long exposition distinguishing tempus absolutum & relativum, spatium absolutum & relativum, locus, motus absolutus & relativus, and their properties and interrelations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newton sets out: (I) absolute, true, mathematical time flows uniformly vs relative, apparent time measured by motion (hours/days); (II) absolute space is immovable and persistent vs relative space as measure or position relative to bodies; (III) locus is part of space a body occupies; (IV) absolute vs relative motion and rest and how to distinguish them by causes/effects (forces). He gives examples (ship, rotating water in a bowl) and argues for distinguishing true quantities from sensory measures, and shows how true motion may be inferred from forces and effects (e.g., centrifugal effects, tension in connecting strings, behavior of rotating fluids).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lex. I (First Law) — Inertia
rubrics_metrics.description: Corpus omne perseverare in statu suo quiescendi vel movendi uniformiter in directum, nisi quatenus a viribus impressis cogitur statum illum mutare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States the principle of inertia: bodies maintain rest or uniform straight-line motion unless acted on by impressed forces. Examples: projectiles, pendulums, planets/comets preserving motion in less resisting space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lex. II (Second Law) — Proportionality of change of motion to impressed force
rubrics_metrics.description: Mutationem motus proportionalem esse vi motrici impressæ, & fieri secundum lineam rectam qua vis illa imprimitur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formulates that change in motion (i.e., change in momentum) is proportional to the impressed motive force and occurs in the straight line of its action. Notes additive properties when multiple forces act and composition of velocities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lex. III (Third Law) — Action and reaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Actioni contrariam semper & æqualem esse reactionem: sive corporum duorum actiones in se mutuo semper esse æquales & in partes contrarias dirigi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States that mutual actions between bodies are equal and opposite. Gives intuitive examples (finger pressing stone, horse pulling a stone by rope) and notes that equal actions produce equal changes in motion (momentum) when no other impediments exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary I (Parallelogram composition of forces / motions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Corpus viribus conjunctis diagonalem parallelogrammi eodem tempore describere, quo latera separatis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows composition of two simultaneous actions (forces or motions) results in the diagonal of the parallelogram formed by their separate effects; demonstrates vector composition geometrically and its mechanical confirmation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary II (Composition/resolution of forces; mechanical examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Et hinc patet compositio vis directæ AD ex viribus quibusvis obliquis AB & BD, & vicissim resolutio vis cujusvis directæ AD in obliquas quascunq; AB & BD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expands on composition/resolution of forces with detailed mechanical illustrations (pulleys, levers, radii, weights), derives relations used in machines, inclines, wedges, and screws; applies to analysis of mechanical advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary III (Conservation of quantity of motion under mutual actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantitas motus quæ colligitur capiendo summam motuum factorum ad eandem partem, & differentiam factorum ad contrarias, non mutatur ab actione corporum inter se.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrates that the total quantity of motion (momentum sum/difference) is unchanged by mutual actions of bodies (internal interactions), with examples of collisions and reflections; shows how to compute post-collision motions from pre-collision momenta.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary IV (Center of gravity of system unaffected by internal actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commune gravitatis centrum ab actionibus corporum inter se non mutat statum suum vel motus vel quietis, & propterea corporum omnium in se mutuo agentium (exclusis actionibus & impedimentis externis) commune centrum gravitatis vel quiescit vel movetur uniformiter in directum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States that the center of gravity of a system is not changed in its motion by internal mutual forces; with no external forces, the center of gravity remains at rest or moves uniformly in a straight line. Provides sketch of inductive proof building up from two bodies to many.
